# 🧱 mBlock beginner examples: Ranger 8-Way

[🔙 Back to the Ranger 8-Way product page](/en/sensors/tof8/index.md)

This page is for people who have **never written a program**: read the Ranger 8-Way on an **mBot** with mBlock 5 blocks. The 5 examples start with "turn the number into a sound" and work up to a robot that drives itself. Every example has a block picture, a downloadable project file and an Arduino sketch that does the same thing.

| Software | Who it suits | How to open the example file |
|---|---|---|
| 🟧 **mBlock 5 desktop** (blocks, Upload mode) + **MBC Pro Sensors extension v2** | Schools, first time with an mBot | Download the `.mblock` → open mBlock 5 → "File → Open from your computer" → switch to "Upload" at the bottom right → "Upload" |
| 🔧 **Arduino IDE** (text code) | People who want to see what is behind the blocks, or write their own code | Download the `.ino` → install the Makeblock and MBC_Sensors libraries (see [Makeblock extension](/en/makeblock.md)) → board Arduino Uno → upload |

> [!IMPORTANT]
> - The sensor must be the **Makeblock edition with the 2026-10 protocol v2 firmware**, connected through the **mBot socket board** to an RJ25 port; use extension **v2.0.0** (old firmware goes with the old v1 extension; they cannot be mixed).
> - The board is the **mBot (mCore)**. mBot Ranger, Orion and MegaPi work too: swap "when mBot starts up" for that board's hat block and use a port that board allows (see [supported boards and ports](/en/makeblock.md)); the mBot2 (CyberPi) has no RJ25 port and is not supported.
> - mBlock 5 is shown here with its English block text; your copy may show the same blocks in another language.

## Before you start

<figure class="ref-fig"><img src="/images/figures/tof8/wiring-mbot.svg" alt="Ranger 8-Way × mBot wiring" loading="lazy"></figure>

Sensor → mBot socket board → RJ25 port on the board (S1 = host TX, S2 = host RX, UART 38400).

1. **Install the extension**: get the **MBC Pro Sensors v2.0.0** `.mext` from [Makeblock extension](/en/makeblock.md) and drop it into the mBlock 5 window; add **mBot** under "Devices" (bottom left) and switch to "Upload" (bottom right).
2. **Wiring**: Ranger → mBot socket board → mBot **port 3** (every example on this page uses this port; to use another, change the port number on the blocks).
3. **Let it boot first**: every example starts with "wait 3 seconds" so the sensor can boot; the 8 lasers take 2~4 s to initialise and read 120 meanwhile, which is normal.
4. The Ranger 8-way needs no calibration. The 8 lasers form a half circle: sensor 1 far left, 4 and 5 straight ahead, 8 far right (30° apart); "nearest direction" negative = left, 0 = ahead, positive = right; nothing around reads **120**.
5. **Check left/right with example 2 first**: a hand on the left of the robot must give a red LED; blue means the sensor is mounted reversed and left/right in the later examples will be swapped.

## Blocks used on this page

Each reporter block is one "value id" of the sensor's value table (the same ids as the Arduino I2C registers); the full block list is in [Makeblock extension](/en/makeblock.md).

| Block | Returns | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Ranger 8 port [3] nearest distance cm | 0~120 cm | smallest of the 8 distances, 0~120 cm (a failed sensor counts as 120); 120 = nothing around |
| Ranger 8 port [3] nearest direction | -8~+8 | direction of the nearest object: −7 (left) to +7 (right), 0 = straight ahead, negative = left; ±8 = nothing around (keeps the last side) |
| Ranger 8 port [3] farthest direction | -7~+7 | direction of the most open side: −7 to +7, 0 = straight ahead, negative = left; 0 when all 8 read 120 |

**Examples on this page**

1. [Nearest-distance theremin](#example-1-nearest-distance-theremin)
2. [The LED shows which side the object is on](#example-2-the-led-shows-which-side-the-object-is-on)
3. [One wheel points the robot at the nearest object](#example-3-one-wheel-points-the-robot-at-the-nearest-object)
4. [Obstacle-avoiding drive](#example-4-obstacle-avoiding-drive)
5. [Head for open space](#example-5-head-for-open-space)

> [!NOTE]
> The `.mblock` files are generated in the mBlock 5 save format and **have not yet been opened in mBlock 5 for verification** (pending the extension v2 release). If one will not open or shows blank blocks, check that extension v2 is loaded and the device is mBot, or rebuild it from the block picture below (under 5 minutes); you can also [tell us on LINE](https://line.me/R/ti/p/@692vcvuk).

## Example 1: Nearest-distance theremin

**What this example does**: The mBot has no screen, so this example turns the "nearest distance" (the smallest of the 8, 0 to 120 cm) into a pitch: whichever direction something approaches from, the note drops. Learn to "read the number" first.

**What you need**
- mBot (mCore board) + mBlock 5 desktop
- Ranger 8-Way (Makeblock edition) + mBot socket board

**Wiring**: Ranger → mBot socket board → mBot **port 3**. Mount it at the very front with sensors 4 and 5 facing forward (sensor 1 far left, 8 far right).

**Download**

| mBlock 5 project | Equivalent Arduino sketch |
|---|---|
| [ex01_theremin.mblock](/examples/tof8/mblock/ex01_theremin.mblock) | [ex01_theremin.ino](/examples/tof8/mblock/ex01_theremin/ex01_theremin.ino) |

<details open>
<summary>🧱 mBlock blocks (just rebuild them like this)</summary>

<pre class="blocks">when mBot starts up :: events hat
wait (3) seconds
forever
  play tone ((200) + ((Ranger 8 port [3 v] nearest distance cm :: #0A9E8F) * (10))) Hz for (0.1) seconds :: sound
end</pre>

</details>

<details>
<summary>🔧 Equivalent Arduino sketch (mBot)</summary>

```cpp
// Ranger 8-Way × mBlock 5  Example 1: Nearest-distance theremin  (equivalent Arduino sketch for mBot)
// Wiring: Ranger → mBot socket board → mBot port 3. Mount it at the very front with sensors 4 and 5 facing forward (sensor 1 far left, 8 far right).
// Does exactly what the mBlock block example does, for people who want to see "what is behind the blocks" or use the Arduino IDE.
// Libraries needed:
//   1. Makeblock (Arduino IDE Library Manager, search "Makeblock", or the copy inside the mBlock 5 install folder)
//   2. MBC_Sensors v2: the four files in src/ of the extension .mext (MBC_Sensors.h/.cpp, mbc_proto.h, mbc_ids.h),
//      put them in Documents/Arduino/libraries/MBC_Sensors/ and #include <MBC_Sensors.h> (https://mbc-pro-sensors.github.io/en/makeblock.html)
// Board: Arduino Uno (the mBot mCore is an Uno). After uploading, unplug USB and run on battery.

#include <MeMCore.h>            // mBot (mCore): motors, LED, buzzer
#include <SoftwareSerial.h>
#include <MBC_Sensors.h>        // MBC sensors v2 (the same library the mBlock extension uses)

MBCPort mbc_port3(3);           // sensor on mBot port 3
MeDCMotor motorL(9);           // left wheel (M1)
MeDCMotor motorR(10);          // right wheel (M2)
MeRGBLed rgbled(7, 2);         // on-board RGB LED (2 pixels)
MeBuzzer buzzer;               // on-board buzzer

// left / right wheel power -100~100 (positive = forward): the mBot left wheel is mounted mirrored, so M1 gets the negative value; % becomes PWM 0~255
void wheels(int l, int r) {
  l = constrain(l, -100, 100); r = constrain(r, -100, 100);
  motorL.run(-l * 255 / 100);
  motorR.run(r * 255 / 100);
}

void setup() {   // everything runs inside setup(), just like the program mBlock generates
  mbc_port3.begin();
  delay(3000);   // Wait 3 s for the 8 lasers to initialise
  while (1) {   // Repeat forever
    buzzer.tone((200 + (mbcRead(mbc_port3, 0x01) * 10)), 100);   // Pitch = 200 + nearest distance × 10 Hz, for 0.1 s
  }
}

void loop() {}   // nothing here: the blocks above never return
```

</details>

**Step by step**
1. Wait 3 s for the 8 lasers to initialise
2. Repeat forever
   - Pitch = 200 + nearest distance × 10 Hz, for 0.1 s

**What you should see**: Nothing around: a high 1400 Hz. Approach from the left, front or right and the pitch drops; 300 Hz at 10 cm.

**FAQ**
- **No sound?** → The buzzer is on the board and is not loud; listen closely, or change 0.1 s to 0.3 s.
- **Low note right after power-on?** → During the first 3 s the lasers initialise and read 120 (high note). A constant low note means something is near (table, wall); give the robot more room.
- **Left and right are swapped?** → The sensor is mounted upside down or rotated 180°. Check with example 2: a hand on the left of the robot must give a red LED.
- **Nothing happens, or the value stays at -32768?** → Wrong port (every example on this page uses port 3), socket board not seated, or the sensor is not the Makeblock edition. Check with the "MBC common → connected?" block first; "protocol version" must read 2 for the new firmware (old firmware needs extension v1).
- **Upload fails, or the blocks are blank?** → Make sure the switch at the bottom right is in "Upload" mode, extension v2 has been dropped into mBlock, and the USB cable goes to the mBot board.

## Example 2: The LED shows which side the object is on

**What this example does**: "Nearest direction" says where the nearest object is: negative = left, 0 = straight ahead, positive = right. With "if… then… else…": something within 60 cm on the left → red, right → blue, straight ahead → green; nothing → LED off.

**What you need**
- mBot (mCore board) + mBlock 5 desktop
- Ranger 8-Way (Makeblock edition) + mBot socket board

**Wiring**: Ranger → mBot socket board → mBot **port 3**. Mount it at the very front with sensors 4 and 5 facing forward (sensor 1 far left, 8 far right).

**Download**

| mBlock 5 project | Equivalent Arduino sketch |
|---|---|
| [ex02_led_direction.mblock](/examples/tof8/mblock/ex02_led_direction.mblock) | [ex02_led_direction.ino](/examples/tof8/mblock/ex02_led_direction/ex02_led_direction.ino) |

<details open>
<summary>🧱 mBlock blocks (just rebuild them like this)</summary>

<pre class="blocks">when mBot starts up :: events hat
wait (3) seconds
forever
  if &lt;(Ranger 8 port [3 v] nearest distance cm :: #0A9E8F) &gt; (60)&gt; then
    LED [all v] colour red (0) green (0) blue (0) :: looks
  else
    if &lt;(Ranger 8 port [3 v] nearest direction :: #0A9E8F) &lt; (0)&gt; then
      LED [all v] colour red (255) green (0) blue (0) :: looks
    else
      if &lt;(Ranger 8 port [3 v] nearest direction :: #0A9E8F) &gt; (0)&gt; then
        LED [all v] colour red (0) green (0) blue (255) :: looks
      else
        LED [all v] colour red (0) green (255) blue (0) :: looks
      end
    end
  end
end</pre>

</details>

<details>
<summary>🔧 Equivalent Arduino sketch (mBot)</summary>

```cpp
// Ranger 8-Way × mBlock 5  Example 2: The LED shows which side the object is on  (equivalent Arduino sketch for mBot)
// Wiring: Ranger → mBot socket board → mBot port 3. Mount it at the very front with sensors 4 and 5 facing forward (sensor 1 far left, 8 far right).
// Does exactly what the mBlock block example does, for people who want to see "what is behind the blocks" or use the Arduino IDE.
// Libraries needed:
//   1. Makeblock (Arduino IDE Library Manager, search "Makeblock", or the copy inside the mBlock 5 install folder)
//   2. MBC_Sensors v2: the four files in src/ of the extension .mext (MBC_Sensors.h/.cpp, mbc_proto.h, mbc_ids.h),
//      put them in Documents/Arduino/libraries/MBC_Sensors/ and #include <MBC_Sensors.h> (https://mbc-pro-sensors.github.io/en/makeblock.html)
// Board: Arduino Uno (the mBot mCore is an Uno). After uploading, unplug USB and run on battery.

#include <MeMCore.h>            // mBot (mCore): motors, LED, buzzer
#include <SoftwareSerial.h>
#include <MBC_Sensors.h>        // MBC sensors v2 (the same library the mBlock extension uses)

MBCPort mbc_port3(3);           // sensor on mBot port 3
MeDCMotor motorL(9);           // left wheel (M1)
MeDCMotor motorR(10);          // right wheel (M2)
MeRGBLed rgbled(7, 2);         // on-board RGB LED (2 pixels)
MeBuzzer buzzer;               // on-board buzzer

// left / right wheel power -100~100 (positive = forward): the mBot left wheel is mounted mirrored, so M1 gets the negative value; % becomes PWM 0~255
void wheels(int l, int r) {
  l = constrain(l, -100, 100); r = constrain(r, -100, 100);
  motorL.run(-l * 255 / 100);
  motorR.run(r * 255 / 100);
}

void setup() {   // everything runs inside setup(), just like the program mBlock generates
  mbc_port3.begin();
  delay(3000);   // Wait 3 s for the 8 lasers to initialise
  while (1) {   // Repeat forever
    if ((mbcRead(mbc_port3, 0x01) > 60)) {   // If the nearest distance is greater than 60
      rgbled.setColor(0, 0, 0, 0); rgbled.show();   // Nothing within 60 cm: LED off
    } else {
      if ((mbcRead(mbc_port3, 0x02) < 0)) {   // Otherwise, if the nearest direction is less than 0 (left)
        rgbled.setColor(0, 255, 0, 0); rgbled.show();   // Nearest object on the left: red
      } else {
        if ((mbcRead(mbc_port3, 0x02) > 0)) {   // Otherwise, if the nearest direction is greater than 0 (right)
          rgbled.setColor(0, 0, 0, 255); rgbled.show();   // On the right: blue
        } else {
          rgbled.setColor(0, 0, 255, 0); rgbled.show();   // Straight ahead: green
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

void loop() {}   // nothing here: the blocks above never return
```

</details>

**Step by step**
1. Wait 3 s for the 8 lasers to initialise
2. Repeat forever
   - If the nearest distance is greater than 60
      - Nothing within 60 cm: LED off
      - otherwise:
         - Otherwise, if the nearest direction is less than 0 (left)
            - Nearest object on the left: red
            - otherwise:
               - Otherwise, if the nearest direction is greater than 0 (right)
                  - On the right: blue
                  - otherwise:
                     - Straight ahead: green

**What you should see**: Hand on the left of the robot: red; right: blue; straight ahead: green; take it away (beyond 60 cm) and the LED goes off.

**FAQ**
- **Left and right are swapped?** → The sensor is mounted upside down or rotated 180°. Check with example 2: a hand on the left of the robot must give a red LED.
- **Nothing happens, or the value stays at -32768?** → Wrong port (every example on this page uses port 3), socket board not seated, or the sensor is not the Makeblock edition. Check with the "MBC common → connected?" block first; "protocol version" must read 2 for the new firmware (old firmware needs extension v1).
- **Upload fails, or the blocks are blank?** → Make sure the switch at the bottom right is in "Upload" mode, extension v2 has been dropped into mBlock, and the USB cable goes to the mBot board.

## Example 3: One wheel points the robot at the nearest object

**What this example does**: Left wheel only: power = nearest direction × 6. Object on the right (positive) → left wheel forward, nose turns right; on the left (negative) → wheel reverses, nose turns left; straight ahead (0) → still. Nothing within 60 cm → stop. Put it on the floor and watch the nose follow your hand.

**What you need**
- mBot (mCore board) + mBlock 5 desktop
- mBot two-wheel robot (left wheel on M1, right wheel on M2, as shipped)
- Ranger 8-Way (Makeblock edition) + mBot socket board
- A few boxes as obstacles

**Wiring**: Ranger → mBot socket board → mBot **port 3**. Mount it at the very front with sensors 4 and 5 facing forward (sensor 1 far left, 8 far right).

**Download**

| mBlock 5 project | Equivalent Arduino sketch |
|---|---|
| [ex03_one_wheel.mblock](/examples/tof8/mblock/ex03_one_wheel.mblock) | [ex03_one_wheel.ino](/examples/tof8/mblock/ex03_one_wheel/ex03_one_wheel.ino) |

<details open>
<summary>🧱 mBlock blocks (just rebuild them like this)</summary>

<pre class="blocks">when mBot starts up :: events hat
wait (3) seconds
forever
  if &lt;(Ranger 8 port [3 v] nearest distance cm :: #0A9E8F) &gt; (60)&gt; then
    stop moving :: motion
  else
    left wheel power ((Ranger 8 port [3 v] nearest direction :: #0A9E8F) * (6)) %, right wheel power (0) % :: motion
  end
end</pre>

</details>

<details>
<summary>🔧 Equivalent Arduino sketch (mBot)</summary>

```cpp
// Ranger 8-Way × mBlock 5  Example 3: One wheel points the robot at the nearest object  (equivalent Arduino sketch for mBot)
// Wiring: Ranger → mBot socket board → mBot port 3. Mount it at the very front with sensors 4 and 5 facing forward (sensor 1 far left, 8 far right).
// Does exactly what the mBlock block example does, for people who want to see "what is behind the blocks" or use the Arduino IDE.
// Libraries needed:
//   1. Makeblock (Arduino IDE Library Manager, search "Makeblock", or the copy inside the mBlock 5 install folder)
//   2. MBC_Sensors v2: the four files in src/ of the extension .mext (MBC_Sensors.h/.cpp, mbc_proto.h, mbc_ids.h),
//      put them in Documents/Arduino/libraries/MBC_Sensors/ and #include <MBC_Sensors.h> (https://mbc-pro-sensors.github.io/en/makeblock.html)
// Board: Arduino Uno (the mBot mCore is an Uno). After uploading, unplug USB and run on battery.

#include <MeMCore.h>            // mBot (mCore): motors, LED, buzzer
#include <SoftwareSerial.h>
#include <MBC_Sensors.h>        // MBC sensors v2 (the same library the mBlock extension uses)

MBCPort mbc_port3(3);           // sensor on mBot port 3
MeDCMotor motorL(9);           // left wheel (M1)
MeDCMotor motorR(10);          // right wheel (M2)
MeRGBLed rgbled(7, 2);         // on-board RGB LED (2 pixels)
MeBuzzer buzzer;               // on-board buzzer

// left / right wheel power -100~100 (positive = forward): the mBot left wheel is mounted mirrored, so M1 gets the negative value; % becomes PWM 0~255
void wheels(int l, int r) {
  l = constrain(l, -100, 100); r = constrain(r, -100, 100);
  motorL.run(-l * 255 / 100);
  motorR.run(r * 255 / 100);
}

void setup() {   // everything runs inside setup(), just like the program mBlock generates
  mbc_port3.begin();
  delay(3000);   // Wait 3 s for the 8 lasers to initialise
  while (1) {   // Repeat forever
    if ((mbcRead(mbc_port3, 0x01) > 60)) {   // If the nearest distance is greater than 60
      wheels(0, 0);   // Nothing within 60 cm: stop
    } else {
      wheels((mbcRead(mbc_port3, 0x02) * 6), 0);   // Left wheel power = nearest direction × 6 (−42 to +42), right wheel 0
    }
  }
}

void loop() {}   // nothing here: the blocks above never return
```

</details>

**Step by step**
1. Wait 3 s for the 8 lasers to initialise
2. Repeat forever
   - If the nearest distance is greater than 60
      - Nothing within 60 cm: stop
      - otherwise:
         - Left wheel power = nearest direction × 6 (−42 to +42), right wheel 0

**What you should see**: Hand at the front right: the left wheel turns forward and the nose swings toward your hand, stopping when it faces you; move your hand to the left and the wheel reverses.

**FAQ**
- **The robot turns the wrong way and gets worse?** → Swap the "+" and "−" (or swap the left and right wheel powers). The mBot ships with the left wheel on M1 and the right on M2; check your own wiring.
- **Left and right are swapped?** → The sensor is mounted upside down or rotated 180°. Check with example 2: a hand on the left of the robot must give a red LED.
- **Nothing happens, or the value stays at -32768?** → Wrong port (every example on this page uses port 3), socket board not seated, or the sensor is not the Makeblock edition. Check with the "MBC common → connected?" block first; "protocol version" must read 2 for the new firmware (old firmware needs extension v1).
- **Upload fails, or the blocks are blank?** → Make sure the switch at the bottom right is in "Upload" mode, extension v2 has been dropped into mBlock, and the USB cable goes to the mBot board.

## Example 4: Obstacle-avoiding drive

**What this example does**: The robot drives straight; when something is within 20 cm it checks which side: on the left → spin right, on the right (or straight ahead) → spin left, then drives on once the way is clear.

**What you need**
- mBot (mCore board) + mBlock 5 desktop
- mBot two-wheel robot (left wheel on M1, right wheel on M2, as shipped)
- Ranger 8-Way (Makeblock edition) + mBot socket board
- A few boxes as obstacles

**Wiring**: Ranger → mBot socket board → mBot **port 3**. Mount it at the very front with sensors 4 and 5 facing forward (sensor 1 far left, 8 far right).

**Download**

| mBlock 5 project | Equivalent Arduino sketch |
|---|---|
| [ex04_avoid.mblock](/examples/tof8/mblock/ex04_avoid.mblock) | [ex04_avoid.ino](/examples/tof8/mblock/ex04_avoid/ex04_avoid.ino) |

<details open>
<summary>🧱 mBlock blocks (just rebuild them like this)</summary>

<pre class="blocks">when mBot starts up :: events hat
wait (3) seconds
forever
  if &lt;(Ranger 8 port [3 v] nearest distance cm :: #0A9E8F) &lt; (20)&gt; then
    if &lt;(Ranger 8 port [3 v] nearest direction :: #0A9E8F) &lt; (0)&gt; then
      left wheel power (40) %, right wheel power (-40) % :: motion
    else
      left wheel power (-40) %, right wheel power (40) % :: motion
    end
  else
    left wheel power (40) %, right wheel power (40) % :: motion
  end
end</pre>

</details>

<details>
<summary>🔧 Equivalent Arduino sketch (mBot)</summary>

```cpp
// Ranger 8-Way × mBlock 5  Example 4: Obstacle-avoiding drive  (equivalent Arduino sketch for mBot)
// Wiring: Ranger → mBot socket board → mBot port 3. Mount it at the very front with sensors 4 and 5 facing forward (sensor 1 far left, 8 far right).
// Does exactly what the mBlock block example does, for people who want to see "what is behind the blocks" or use the Arduino IDE.
// Libraries needed:
//   1. Makeblock (Arduino IDE Library Manager, search "Makeblock", or the copy inside the mBlock 5 install folder)
//   2. MBC_Sensors v2: the four files in src/ of the extension .mext (MBC_Sensors.h/.cpp, mbc_proto.h, mbc_ids.h),
//      put them in Documents/Arduino/libraries/MBC_Sensors/ and #include <MBC_Sensors.h> (https://mbc-pro-sensors.github.io/en/makeblock.html)
// Board: Arduino Uno (the mBot mCore is an Uno). After uploading, unplug USB and run on battery.

#include <MeMCore.h>            // mBot (mCore): motors, LED, buzzer
#include <SoftwareSerial.h>
#include <MBC_Sensors.h>        // MBC sensors v2 (the same library the mBlock extension uses)

MBCPort mbc_port3(3);           // sensor on mBot port 3
MeDCMotor motorL(9);           // left wheel (M1)
MeDCMotor motorR(10);          // right wheel (M2)
MeRGBLed rgbled(7, 2);         // on-board RGB LED (2 pixels)
MeBuzzer buzzer;               // on-board buzzer

// left / right wheel power -100~100 (positive = forward): the mBot left wheel is mounted mirrored, so M1 gets the negative value; % becomes PWM 0~255
void wheels(int l, int r) {
  l = constrain(l, -100, 100); r = constrain(r, -100, 100);
  motorL.run(-l * 255 / 100);
  motorR.run(r * 255 / 100);
}

void setup() {   // everything runs inside setup(), just like the program mBlock generates
  mbc_port3.begin();
  delay(3000);   // Wait 3 s for the 8 lasers to initialise
  while (1) {   // Repeat forever
    if ((mbcRead(mbc_port3, 0x01) < 20)) {   // If the nearest distance is less than 20
      if ((mbcRead(mbc_port3, 0x02) < 0)) {   // If the nearest direction is less than 0 (left)
        wheels(40, -40);   // Obstacle on the left: spin right
      } else {
        wheels(-40, 40);   // Obstacle on the right or ahead: spin left
      }
    } else {
      wheels(40, 40);   // Clear: drive straight
    }
  }
}

void loop() {}   // nothing here: the blocks above never return
```

</details>

**Step by step**
1. Wait 3 s for the 8 lasers to initialise
2. Repeat forever
   - If the nearest distance is less than 20
      - If the nearest direction is less than 0 (left)
         - Obstacle on the left: spin right
         - otherwise:
            - Obstacle on the right or ahead: spin left
      - otherwise:
         - Clear: drive straight

**What you should see**: The robot weaves between the boxes, turning away before it touches anything.

**FAQ**
- **It scrapes boxes with its side?** → The side lasers (1 and 8) count toward "nearest distance"; raise 20 (e.g. to 30) to keep more clearance.
- **The robot turns the wrong way and gets worse?** → Swap the "+" and "−" (or swap the left and right wheel powers). The mBot ships with the left wheel on M1 and the right on M2; check your own wiring.
- **Left and right are swapped?** → The sensor is mounted upside down or rotated 180°. Check with example 2: a hand on the left of the robot must give a red LED.
- **Nothing happens, or the value stays at -32768?** → Wrong port (every example on this page uses port 3), socket board not seated, or the sensor is not the Makeblock edition. Check with the "MBC common → connected?" block first; "protocol version" must read 2 for the new firmware (old firmware needs extension v1).
- **Upload fails, or the blocks are blank?** → Make sure the switch at the bottom right is in "Upload" mode, extension v2 has been dropped into mBlock, and the USB cable goes to the mBot board.

## Example 5: Head for open space

**What this example does**: Example 4 only turns when it meets something; this one steers toward the "farthest direction" as it drives: turn = farthest direction × 6, left wheel 35 + turn, right wheel 35 − turn, so the robot drifts around obstacles toward the widest space (green LED). If something is really close (within 10 cm) it backs up with a red LED.

**What you need**
- mBot (mCore board) + mBlock 5 desktop
- mBot two-wheel robot (left wheel on M1, right wheel on M2, as shipped)
- Ranger 8-Way (Makeblock edition) + mBot socket board
- A few boxes as obstacles

**Wiring**: Ranger → mBot socket board → mBot **port 3**. Mount it at the very front with sensors 4 and 5 facing forward (sensor 1 far left, 8 far right).

<details>
<summary>🔧 Equivalent Arduino sketch (mBot)</summary>

```cpp
// Ranger 8-Way × mBlock 5  Example 5: Head for open space  (equivalent Arduino sketch for mBot)
// Wiring: Ranger → mBot socket board → mBot port 3. Mount it at the very front with sensors 4 and 5 facing forward (sensor 1 far left, 8 far right).
// Does exactly what the mBlock block example does, for people who want to see "what is behind the blocks" or use the Arduino IDE.
// Libraries needed:
//   1. Makeblock (Arduino IDE Library Manager, search "Makeblock", or the copy inside the mBlock 5 install folder)
//   2. MBC_Sensors v2: the four files in src/ of the extension .mext (MBC_Sensors.h/.cpp, mbc_proto.h, mbc_ids.h),
//      put them in Documents/Arduino/libraries/MBC_Sensors/ and #include <MBC_Sensors.h> (https://mbc-pro-sensors.github.io/en/makeblock.html)
// Board: Arduino Uno (the mBot mCore is an Uno). After uploading, unplug USB and run on battery.

#include <MeMCore.h>            // mBot (mCore): motors, LED, buzzer
#include <SoftwareSerial.h>
#include <MBC_Sensors.h>        // MBC sensors v2 (the same library the mBlock extension uses)

MBCPort mbc_port3(3);           // sensor on mBot port 3
MeDCMotor motorL(9);           // left wheel (M1)
MeDCMotor motorR(10);          // right wheel (M2)
MeRGBLed rgbled(7, 2);         // on-board RGB LED (2 pixels)
MeBuzzer buzzer;               // on-board buzzer
float turn = 0;               // variable：turn

// left / right wheel power -100~100 (positive = forward): the mBot left wheel is mounted mirrored, so M1 gets the negative value; % becomes PWM 0~255
void wheels(int l, int r) {
  l = constrain(l, -100, 100); r = constrain(r, -100, 100);
  motorL.run(-l * 255 / 100);
  motorR.run(r * 255 / 100);
}

void setup() {   // everything runs inside setup(), just like the program mBlock generates
  mbc_port3.begin();
  delay(3000);   // Wait 3 s for the 8 lasers to initialise
  while (1) {   // Repeat forever
    if ((mbcRead(mbc_port3, 0x01) < 10)) {   // If the nearest distance is less than 10
      rgbled.setColor(0, 255, 0, 0); rgbled.show();   // Too close: red LED
      wheels(-30, -30);   // Back up
    } else {
      rgbled.setColor(0, 0, 255, 0); rgbled.show();   // Green LED
      turn = (mbcRead(mbc_port3, 0x04) * 6);   // turn = farthest direction × 6 (−42 to +42)
      wheels((35 + turn), (35 - turn));   // Left = 35 + turn, right = 35 − turn: open space on the left (negative) → left wheel slow, drift left
    }
  }
}

void loop() {}   // nothing here: the blocks above never return
```

</details>

**Step by step**
1. Wait 3 s for the 8 lasers to initialise
2. Repeat forever
   - If the nearest distance is less than 10
      - Too close: red LED
      - Back up
      - otherwise:
         - Green LED
         - turn = farthest direction × 6 (−42 to +42)
         - Left = 35 + turn, right = 35 − turn: open space on the left (negative) → left wheel slow, drift left

**What you should see**: The robot keeps heading for the most open direction, steering around boxes early; when boxed in it backs up with a red LED.

**FAQ**
- **The robot keeps swinging left and right?** → Lower × 6 (e.g. × 4).
- **The robot turns the wrong way and gets worse?** → Swap the "+" and "−" (or swap the left and right wheel powers). The mBot ships with the left wheel on M1 and the right on M2; check your own wiring.
- **Left and right are swapped?** → The sensor is mounted upside down or rotated 180°. Check with example 2: a hand on the left of the robot must give a red LED.
- **Nothing happens, or the value stays at -32768?** → Wrong port (every example on this page uses port 3), socket board not seated, or the sensor is not the Makeblock edition. Check with the "MBC common → connected?" block first; "protocol version" must read 2 for the new firmware (old firmware needs extension v1).
- **Upload fails, or the blocks are blank?** → Make sure the switch at the bottom right is in "Upload" mode, extension v2 has been dropped into mBlock, and the USB cable goes to the mBot board.
